HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Habeas Corpus Petition No. 22 of 2021
Bridjet Spencer …........ Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others …..... Respondents
Present : Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate for the petitioner. 
 Mr. Pratiroop Pandey and Lalit Miglani, A.G.As. with Ms. Sonika and 
 Ms. Lata Negi, Brief Holders for the State of Uttarakhand.
 Mr. Gopal Kumar Verma, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar 
 Pradesh. 
 
 
JUDGMENT 
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
This is a habeas corpus petition. Petitioner 
claims that she is in live-in relationship with Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav S/o Mr. Harish Chandra Yadav, who has 
been confined in Vikalp Nasha Mukti Evam Punarwas 
Kendra, near State Bank, Delhi Road, Pakbara, District 
Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. According to the petitioner, 
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav has been illegally detained by the 
respondent no.6-Center, at the behest of the respondent 
no.5, who is father-in-law of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. 
2. On 25.11.2021, this Court directed the 
respondent no.4 to retrieve the corpus of Mr. Vikas Singh 
Yadav and produce him before this Court. Mr. Vikas  2
Singh Yadav is present before this Court as identified by 
Mr. B.C. Joshi, Sub-Inspector, Police Station Bhimtal, 
District Naintial. He is also accompanied by Mr. Mukesh 
Rajora, Sub-Inspector, Police Station Pakbara, District 
Moradabad. Director of the Vikalp Nasha Mukti Evam 
Punarwas Kendra, Mr. Mohd. Parvez is also present 
before this Court.
3. The Court questioned Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav, 
he would submit as hereunder:-
(i) I was practicing Advocate in the High Court of 
Uttarakhand, Nainital. My in-laws and my 
family members lodged a missing report at 
Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad. On 
03.09.2021, my in-laws took me from Bhimtal 
and to Moradabad. On the same night, my in￾laws pressurized me that I should stay in 
Moradabad. They snatched my mobile phone, 
my ID Cards, my ID of Nainital High Court, 
they also took `4,500/- from me. 
(ii) On the next day, they handed me over to Mr. 
Parvez. I was handed over at Reliance Petrol 
Pump, Delhi Road, Moradabad. Thereafter, Mr.  3
Mohd. Parvez along with the two persons, took 
me in their Nasha Mukti Center. On the same 
day, they asked me to sign on a file. For the 
last three months, I am confined in that 
Center. I do not get any sun light. I have been 
facing physical and mental torture. I have been 
living in a very unhygienic condition in the 
center. In the center, in an area of about 2000 
square feet, they had confined about 90 
persons in the last month and this month, 
there are 60 persons; they are kept like 
animals. I was 85 Kilograms, when I entered 
the Center, today perhaps I have reduced to 65 
Kilograms.
(iii) In their Center, there is a Sanjivini Booti, if 
anyone has any problem with any person, 
either with regard to property or someone 
wants to evade the police, or with regard to 
their family matters, the person may be sent to 
this Center. All the problems are resolved. The 
Center people would not reveal the information 
about the inmates, those who are confined in 
the Center. In fact, in my case also, the  4
petitioner was searching for me and initially the 
Center people denied my admission in the 
Center. I was never medically examined. I never 
saw any doctor in the Center. In the Center,
they do not provide adequate food. In the 
Center, they also give special punishment and 
for that purpose they would lower the pants 
and would beat with chappal and danda. For 
that purpose they had identified the places 
which are not covered by CCTV cameras. There 
was an inmate named Robin Massih. I was told 
that he was fine, when he was taken to the 
Center, but on 24th or 26th of November, 2021, 
his condition was deteriorated. The Center 
people contemplating his imminent death, got 
him admitted in the hospital, where he died a 
day thereafter. I was told that Robin Massih’s 
sister got him admitted there because she 
wanted the share in the property, as Robin 
Massih was unmarried. 
(iv) The Center keeps people there for a longer 
time. In fact there are persons, who have been 
detained in the Center for more than 13  5
months now. I can even name them. A Shabaz 
is there for the last 13 months. He is a resident 
of Baheri, perhaps it is in District Bareilly. One 
Mohd. Sajman is confined in the Center for the 
last 09 months. He is resident of District 
Bijnor. One Mr. Asad Khan from District 
Sambhal has been in the Center for almost 11 
years now. He was released for one month or 
two months and again called at the Center. 
4. Mr. Mohd. Parvez, the Director of Vikalp Nasha 
Mukti Evam Punarwas Kendra, the respondent no.6 is 
present before the Court. The Court wanted to know from 
him, as to how they are running the Center. The Court 
also wanted to know from him, as to what is the basis of 
confining Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav in the Center?
Particularly, as to whether he has ever been medically 
examined by any doctor to certify that he is a person to be 
kept in the Center. 
5. According to Mr. Mohd. Parvez, Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav was never examined by any doctor before he 
was taken in the Center. According to him, his family 
members handed Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav to him,  6
therefore, they took him in the Center. It was told that 
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was a Smack addict. 
6. On the further query of the Court, as to 
whether Mr. Mohd. Parvez, the Director of the Center, has 
ever got Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav examined from the doctor 
to ascertain, as to whether he is mentally ill or to confirm 
he is a person fit to be confined in the Center? He replied 
that such medical examination was never done. In fact, 
Mr. Mohd. Parvez has placed a purported prescription 
given by a doctor, Rekha Dhariwal, Pakbara Clinic, 
District Moradabad to suggest that the doctor had once
examined Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. This prescription be 
kept on record. It is in two pages. It records that Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav is a Smack addict. 
7. The question is how a doctor at the first 
instance can diagnose that a person is Smack addict?
What procedure had been done? What investigation had 
been carried out? How was it ascertained by the doctor 
that a person is addict? There is no reply to it. 
8. Mr. Mohd. Parvez has also placed before the 
Court a Registration No.67/SMHA/2021-22 dated 
29.06.2021, which is a Provisional Registration given  7
under Section 65(2) or Section 66(10) of the Mental 
Healthcare Act, 2017 (for short, “the Act”), to run Apna 
Vikalp Nasha Mukti Avam Puranavas Kendra and this 
certificate records that number of beds should be 20. The 
Court wanted to know from Mr. Mohd. Parvez, as to how 
against 20 beds, they are taking 60 people or 90 people. 
To it, Mohd. Parvez replied that the persons, who cannot 
pay money, they are also detained in excess to 20.
9. During the course of hearing, Mr. Pratiroop 
Pandey, learned AGA for the State of Uttarakhand, would 
suggests that a person cannot be confined in mental 
health establishment merely on the recommendations of 
the family members. It is barred under Section 3 of the 
Act. He has referred to Section 3(5) of the Act, which 
reads as hereunder:-
“3. Determination of mental illness.-
(1) …………………………………………………………………
(2) …………………………………………………………………
(3) …………………………………………………………………
(4) …………………………………………………………………
(5) The determination of a person's mental illness shall 
alone not imply or be taken to mean that the person is 
of unsound mind unless he has been declared as such 
by a competent court.”
10. Learned State counsel also submits that there 
have been various guidelines of the Court that regulate 
the entry of persons in the mental health establishment.  8
11. Mr. Lalit Miglani, learned AGA for the State of 
Uttarakhand would submit that the State of affairs, as 
disclosed by Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav are very serious and 
in this matter, an FIR should be immediately lodged and 
the inmates should be rescued. 
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner would 
submit that the petitioner should be freed to move 
wherever he wants to move. He would submit that under 
Section 55 of the Act, the State should have supervised
the mental health establishment, which according to the 
learned counsel for the petitioner, it appears has not been 
done. 
13. During the course of hearing, a woman 
introduced herself Smt. Premlata Yadav wife of Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav intervened. She has stated that Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav’s activities are quite strange. He was staying 
with a woman in Mehra Gaon, District Nainital. They 
found 2 ml. syringes from his possession. His behavior 
towards with the family members was bad. They thought 
that he is taking drugs or the woman with whom he is 
staying, is giving him drugs. Therefore, Vikas Singh Yadav 
has been handed over to Mr. Mohd. Parvez. He needs  9
treatment. He is not fit. There are dark patches below his 
eyes; which were not there earlier. 
14. The Court is only concerned now with the 
safety of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. He may not be detained. 
At present he shall not be sent to the respondent no.6 
Center. But, his health condition (especially mental 
health) needs to be examined before he is freed. In case 
doctors advise that Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav needs special 
care, the matter may then be considered accordingly. 
Therefore, before proceeding further in the matter this 
Court shall now separately direct examination of Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav by doctors. Once report is received,
the matter shall be taken up at 04:00 PM today. 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 30.11.2021 Sanjay

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Habeas Corpus Petition No. 22 of 2021
Bridjet Spencer …........ Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others …..... Respondents
Present : Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate for the petitioner. 
 Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Brief Holder for the State of 
 Uttarakhand/respondent nos.1, 2 and 4.
 Mr. Gopal Kumar Verma, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar 
 Pradesh/respondent no.3.
 Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for respondent nos.5 and 6.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
In the instant habeas corpus petition,
directions have been sought to produce the corpus of Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav, who was confined in the Vikalp Nasha 
Mukti Evam Punarwas Kendra, Near State Bank, Delhi 
Road, Pakbara, District Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
(Respondent no.6, hereinafter referred to as, “the 
Centre”). 
2. This Court directed that the corpus of Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav be produced before the Court. On 
30.11.2021, Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was produced before 
the Court. The Court questioned him and his reply has 
been noted in the first order, passed by this Court on 
30.11.2021, which is as hereunder:-
“3. The Court questioned Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav, he 
would submit as hereunder:- 2
(i) I was practicing Advocate in the High Court of 
Uttarakhand, Nainital. My in-laws and my family 
members lodged a missing report at Police Station 
Majhola, District Moradabad. On 03.09.2021, my in￾laws took me from Bhimtal and to Moradabad. On the 
same night, my in-laws pressurized me that I should 
stay in Moradabad. They snatched my mobile phone, 
my ID Cards, my ID of Nainital High Court, they also 
took `4,500/- from me. 
(ii) On the next day, they handed me over to Mr. Parvez. I 
was handed over at Reliance Petrol Pump, Delhi Road, 
Moradabad. Thereafter, Mr. Mohd. Parvez along with the 
two persons, took me in their Nasha Mukti Centre. On 
the same day, they asked me to sign on a file. For the 
last three months, I am confined in that Centre. I do not 
get any sun light. I have been facing physical and 
mental torture. I have been living in a very unhygienic 
condition in the Centre. In the Centre, in an area of 
about 2000 square feet, they had confined about 90 
persons in the last month and this month, there are 60 
persons; they are kept like animals. I was 85 Kilograms, 
when I entered the Centre, today perhaps I have 
reduced to 65 Kilograms.
(iii) In their Centre, there is a Sanjivini Booti, if anyone has 
any problem with any person, either with regard to 
property or someone wants to evade the police, or with 
regard to their family matters, the person may be sent 
to this Centre. All the problems are resolved. The Centre
people would not reveal the information about the 
inmates, those who are confined in the Centre. In fact, 
in my case also, the petitioner was searching for me and 
initially the Centre people denied my admission in the 
Centre. I was never medically examined. I never saw any 
doctor in the Centre. In the Centre, they do not provide 
adequate food. In the Centre, they also give special 
punishment and for that purpose they would lower the 
pants and would beat with chappal and danda. For that  3
purpose they had identified the places which are not 
covered by CCTV cameras. There was an inmate named 
Robin Massih. I was told that he was fine, when he was 
taken to the Centre, but on 24th or 26th of November, 
2021, his condition was deteriorated. The Centre people 
contemplating his imminent death, got him admitted in 
the hospital, where he died a day thereafter. I was told 
that Robin Massih’s sister got him admitted there 
because she wanted the share in the property, as Robin 
Massih was unmarried. 
(iv) The Centre keeps people there for a longer time. In fact 
there are persons, who have been detained in the 
Centre for more than 13 months now. I can even name 
them. A Shabaz is there for the last 13 months. He is a 
resident of Baheri, perhaps it is in District Bareilly. One 
Mohd. Sajman is confined in the Centre for the last 09 
months. He is resident of District Bijnor. One Mr. Asad 
Khan from District Sambhal has been in the Centre for 
almost 11 years now. He was released for one month or 
two months and again called at the Centre. ”
3. When Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was produced, 
his wife also appeared before the Court and claimed that 
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav is unwell. The Centre was also 
represented through its Director Mohd. Parvez. It was told 
on behalf of the Centre by Mohd. Parvez that Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav is a Smack addict and he has been handed 
over to Mohd. Parvez by his family members. The Court, 
thereafter, in para 14 of its first order observed as 
hereunder:- 4
“14. The Court is only concerned now with the 
safety of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. He may not be 
detained. At present he shall not be sent to the 
respondent no.6 Centre. But, his health condition 
(especially mental health) needs to be examined before 
he is freed. In case doctors advise that Mr. Vikas Singh 
Yadav needs special care, the matter may then be 
considered accordingly. Therefore, before proceeding 
further in the matter this Court shall now separately 
direct examination of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav by 
doctors. Once report is received, the matter shall be 
taken up at 04:00 PM today.”
4. Accordingly, on the same day, directions were 
issued for medical examination of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. 
A report was received and the Chief Medical 
Superintendent, B.D. Pandey District Hospital, Mallital, 
Nainital recommended that Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav should 
undergo thorough examination through panel of doctors 
in Medical College Haldwani, District Nainital. It was so 
directed. 
5. Today report is received from Medical College 
Haldwani, District Nainital. According to it, there is no 
psychiatric disorder to Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. 
6. Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav is free to move,
wherever he wants.  5
7. The habeas corpus petition is allowed 
accordingly. 
8. The question is, whether the Court should stop 
here? Or should the Court examine issues, which have 
been raised in the matter? 
9. Today, learned counsel for the petitioner would 
submit that in the affairs of the Centre a detailed inquiry 
should be ordered by the State of Uttar Pradesh, as per 
the provisions of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 (for 
short, “the Act”), which provides punishments also under 
Chapter XV of the Act.
10. Learned counsel representing the State of Uttar 
Pradesh (the respondent no.3, SSP Moradabad) would 
submit that it is a very serious matter; the Centre, it 
appears, has violated the condition of the registration. 
11. Learned counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh 
would submit that he would write to the concerned 
authorities, so that the matter may be looked into. 
12. Learned counsel appearing for the State of 
Uttarakhand would submit that it is a serious matter, in 
which, FIR must be lodged. He also submits that, in fact,  6
there have been instances of irregularities or atrocities 
allegedly done in the Mental Healthcare Institutions in the 
State of Uttarakhand. He would refer to some incidents of 
Dehradun, where according to him, two girls ran away 
from a rehabilitation Centre and when they were 
apprehended, they refused to be admitted in the 
rehabilitation Centre on the ground that they were 
sexually assaulted in the rehabilitation centre. 
13. During the course of hearing, Mrs. Premlata 
Yadav, who introduced herself as the wife of Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav also intervened. 
14. Today, Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, learned counsel 
representing Mrs. Pramlata Yadav would submit that Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav had signed the form for his admission 
in the Centre.
15. At it, Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav has responded 
that he was forced to sign inside the Centre; he had not 
willingly signed it. 
16. Generally this Court should refrain from 
making any observation with regard to the conduct of any 
institution, individual or the system. But, this Court 
would be failing in its duty if this Court does not observe 7
as to what happened during the hearing of this case. On 
30.11.2021, when corpus of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was 
produced before the Court, the Court wanted to see the 
documents maintained by Mohd. Parvez, the respondent 
no.6 with regard to Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. There was a 
discharge form in it, which was though signed, but not 
filled up. Today, when this Court again asked Mohd. 
Parvez, to produce that document. Mohd. Pravez 
produced the same form, but now it is filled up. 
17. The Court asked Mohd. Parvez, as to when was 
it filled up? He would reply that it was filled up yesterday. 
It speaks in volume. This Court leaves it at it. 
18. In fact, on 30.11.2021, Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav 
has stated that he was never examined by any doctor in 
the Centre. He has also told that there are many persons, 
who have been confined in the Centre for many months. 
He has named them and that was recorded in the order 
passed on that day.
19. On 30.11.2021 itself, on behalf of the State of 
Uttarakhand, a report was submitted, which was 
presented by Mr. Mukesh Rajora, Sub-Inspector, Police 
Station Pakbara, District Moradabad, which revealed that  8
on that day, there were 65 persons in the Centre. The 
Centre is registered with 20 number of beds.
20. The laudable object for enacting the Act need 
no reiteration. Mental illness is not something strange, it 
is like any other illness. The Act has intended to give 
dignity to the persons suffering from mental illness; the 
Act has further respected the dignity and privacy of a 
person suffering from mental illness; the Act has further 
regulated the admission of the persons in Mental 
Healthcare Establishment. There are specific provisions 
which deals with it. It may be a hazardous situation, if a 
person sound in mind without any mental illness, is 
confined in any institution or home or where persons with 
mental illness are confined. 
21. This Court in the case of Dr. Vijay Verma vs. 
Union of India and others, (2018) SCC Online 
Uttarakhand 519, has considered the implementation 
aspect of the Act in the State of Uttarakhand and in para 
52 of its judgment, number of directions have been given. 
What happened to those directions? 
22. Though the issue, at present, does not belong 
to the State of Uttarakhand, but reference has been made  9
to the incidents in District Dehradun and it is submitted 
on behalf of the learned counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand itself that this Court should examine the 
implementation aspect of the Act in the State of 
Uttarakhand. This Court considers to examine that 
aspect, as well.
23. The corpus Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was 
detained by the Centre in contravention of the provisions 
of the Act. He had to remain for almost three months in 
the Centre. This act of the respondent no.6 may not be 
termed as a mistake. It is a question of liberty of a person 
snatched without in accordance with law. Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav has narrated the story of inhuman treatment 
and living conditions in the Centre. This Court does not 
know how far is that true. It may definitely be a matter of 
inquiry.
24. In view of the above, the Court issues the 
following directions:-
(i) The respondent no.3, SSP Moradabad, 
Uttar Pradesh shall conduct a detailed 
inquiry with regard to the working of the 
Centre. Let he be provided a copy of the 
paper-book and copies of all the 
documents, which have been given by  10
Mohd. Parvez on 30.11.2021 and the 
documents, which have been taken today 
in custody by this Court from Mohd. 
Parvez. After inquiry, respondent no.3, 
SSP Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh shall 
recommend action as permissible under 
law, including taking legal action against 
the persons, who are found to have
violated the provisions of the Act. 
(ii) The respondent no.6, Centre shall show 
cause, as to why the Centre should not be 
asked to award compensation to Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav for confining him for 
about three months in contravention of 
the provisions of law. 
(iii) Principal Secretary, Health, State of 
Uttarakhand, shall submit the followings;
(a) What action was taken by the State 
of Uttarakhand, pursuant to the 
directions issued by this Court in 
the case of Dr. Vijay Verma (supra).
(b) A list of such Mental Health 
Establishment, registered under 
the Act including any Centre in the 
name of Nasha Mukti Kendra, 
Rehabilitation Centre, etc. The list 
shall also contain the last three 
dates, when under Section 55 of  11
the Act, the State Authority 
supervised such establishments.
(c) When, in the last one year the 
meetings, of the State Authority,
constituted under the Act, took 
place. A copy of the resolutions of 
the State Authority shall also be 
enclosed. 
(iv) The Court also requests the respondent 
no.3 SSP Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh to 
submit a report of the action taken by him 
pursuant to this order. 
25. Let a copy of this order be sent to the Principal 
Secretary, Home, the State of Uttarakhand and Principal 
Secretary, Home, the State of Uttar Pradesh for ensuring 
that the provisions of the Act are implemented in the 
letter and spirt. 
26. The Court requests Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate,
who has represented the petitioner in the case, to assist 
the Court in the matter as Amicus Curiae, once reports 
are submitted. 
27. The matter remains part-heard.
28. The reports from Principal Secretary, State of 
Uttarakhand, SSP Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and show  12
cause, to be submitted by the respondent no.6, shall be 
submitted on or before 15.02.2022. It shall be submitted 
in duplicate. Once it is submitted, a copy of it, shall be 
handed over to the learned Amicus Curiae.
29. List this matter on 18.02.2022 at 02:00 PM.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)

been noted in the first order, passed by this Court on 
30.11.2021, which is as hereunder:-
“3. The Court questioned Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav, he 
would submit as hereunder:- 2
(i) I was practicing Advocate in the High Court of 
Uttarakhand, Nainital. My in-laws and my family 
members lodged a missing report at Police Station 
Majhola, District Moradabad. On 03.09.2021, my in￾laws took me from Bhimtal and to Moradabad. On the 
same night, my in-laws pressurized me that I should 
stay in Moradabad. They snatched my mobile phone, 
my ID Cards, my ID of Nainital High Court, they also 
took `4,500/- from me. 
(ii) On the next day, they handed me over to Mr. Parvez. I 
was handed over at Reliance Petrol Pump, Delhi Road, 
Moradabad. Thereafter, Mr. Mohd. Parvez along with the 
two persons, took me in their Nasha Mukti Centre. On 
the same day, they asked me to sign on a file. For the 
last three months, I am confined in that Centre. I do not 
get any sun light. I have been facing physical and 
mental torture. I have been living in a very unhygienic 
condition in the Centre. In the Centre, in an area of 
about 2000 square feet, they had confined about 90 
persons in the last month and this month, there are 60 
persons; they are kept like animals. I was 85 Kilograms, 
when I entered the Centre, today perhaps I have 
reduced to 65 Kilograms.
(iii) In their Centre, there is a Sanjivini Booti, if anyone has 
any problem with any person, either with regard to 
property or someone wants to evade the police, or with 
regard to their family matters, the person may be sent 
to this Centre. All the problems are resolved. The Centre
people would not reveal the information about the 
inmates, those who are confined in the Centre. In fact, 
in my case also, the petitioner was searching for me and 
initially the Centre people denied my admission in the 
Centre. I was never medically examined. I never saw any 
doctor in the Centre. In the Centre, they do not provide 
adequate food. In the Centre, they also give special 
punishment and for that purpose they would lower the 
pants and would beat with chappal and danda. For that  3
purpose they had identified the places which are not 
covered by CCTV cameras. There was an inmate named 
Robin Massih. I was told that he was fine, when he was 
taken to the Centre, but on 24th or 26th of November, 
2021, his condition was deteriorated. The Centre people 
contemplating his imminent death, got him admitted in 
the hospital, where he died a day thereafter. I was told 
that Robin Massih’s sister got him admitted there 
because she wanted the share in the property, as Robin 
Massih was unmarried. 
(iv) The Centre keeps people there for a longer time. In fact 
there are persons, who have been detained in the 
Centre for more than 13 months now. I can even name 
them. A Shabaz is there for the last 13 months. He is a 
resident of Baheri, perhaps it is in District Bareilly. One 
Mohd. Sajman is confined in the Centre for the last 09 
months. He is resident of District Bijnor. One Mr. Asad 
Khan from District Sambhal has been in the Centre for 
almost 11 years now. He was released for one month or 
two months and again called at the Centre. ”
3. When Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was produced, 
his wife also appeared before the Court and claimed that 
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav is unwell. The Centre was also 
represented through its Director Mohd. Parvez. It was told 
on behalf of the Centre by Mohd. Parvez that Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav is a Smack addict and he has been handed 
over to Mohd. Parvez by his family members. The Court, 
thereafter, in para 14 of its first order observed as 
hereunder:- 4
“14. The Court is only concerned now with the 
safety of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. He may not be 
detained. At present he shall not be sent to the 
respondent no.6 Centre. But, his health condition 
(especially mental health) needs to be examined before 
he is freed. In case doctors advise that Mr. Vikas Singh 
Yadav needs special care, the matter may then be 
considered accordingly. Therefore, before proceeding 
further in the matter this Court shall now separately 
direct examination of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav by 
doctors. Once report is received, the matter shall be 
taken up at 04:00 PM today.”
4. Accordingly, on the same day, directions were 
issued for medical examination of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. 
A report was received and the Chief Medical 
Superintendent, B.D. Pandey District Hospital, Mallital, 
Nainital recommended that Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav should 
undergo thorough examination through panel of doctors 
in Medical College Haldwani, District Nainital. It was so 
directed. 
5. Today report is received from Medical College 
Haldwani, District Nainital. According to it, there is no 
psychiatric disorder to Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. 
6. Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav is free to move,
wherever he wants.  5
7. The habeas corpus petition is allowed 
accordingly. 
8. The question is, whether the Court should stop 
here? Or should the Court examine issues, which have 
been raised in the matter? 
9. Today, learned counsel for the petitioner would 
submit that in the affairs of the Centre a detailed inquiry 
should be ordered by the State of Uttar Pradesh, as per 
the provisions of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 (for 
short, “the Act”), which provides punishments also under 
Chapter XV of the Act.
10. Learned counsel representing the State of Uttar 
Pradesh (the respondent no.3, SSP Moradabad) would 
submit that it is a very serious matter; the Centre, it 
appears, has violated the condition of the registration. 
11. Learned counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh 
would submit that he would write to the concerned 
authorities, so that the matter may be looked into. 
12. Learned counsel appearing for the State of 
Uttarakhand would submit that it is a serious matter, in 
which, FIR must be lodged. He also submits that, in fact,  6
there have been instances of irregularities or atrocities 
allegedly done in the Mental Healthcare Institutions in the 
State of Uttarakhand. He would refer to some incidents of 
Dehradun, where according to him, two girls ran away 
from a rehabilitation Centre and when they were 
apprehended, they refused to be admitted in the 
rehabilitation Centre on the ground that they were 
sexually assaulted in the rehabilitation centre. 
13. During the course of hearing, Mrs. Premlata 
Yadav, who introduced herself as the wife of Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav also intervened. 
14. Today, Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, learned counsel 
representing Mrs. Pramlata Yadav would submit that Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav had signed the form for his admission 
in the Centre.
15. At it, Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav has responded 
that he was forced to sign inside the Centre; he had not 
willingly signed it. 
16. Generally this Court should refrain from 
making any observation with regard to the conduct of any 
institution, individual or the system. But, this Court 
would be failing in its duty if this Court does not observe 7
as to what happened during the hearing of this case. On 
30.11.2021, when corpus of Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was 
produced before the Court, the Court wanted to see the 
documents maintained by Mohd. Parvez, the respondent 
no.6 with regard to Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav. There was a 
discharge form in it, which was though signed, but not 
filled up. Today, when this Court again asked Mohd. 
Parvez, to produce that document. Mohd. Pravez 
produced the same form, but now it is filled up. 
17. The Court asked Mohd. Parvez, as to when was 
it filled up? He would reply that it was filled up yesterday. 
It speaks in volume. This Court leaves it at it. 
18. In fact, on 30.11.2021, Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav 
has stated that he was never examined by any doctor in 
the Centre. He has also told that there are many persons, 
who have been confined in the Centre for many months. 
He has named them and that was recorded in the order 
passed on that day.
19. On 30.11.2021 itself, on behalf of the State of 
Uttarakhand, a report was submitted, which was 
presented by Mr. Mukesh Rajora, Sub-Inspector, Police 
Station Pakbara, District Moradabad, which revealed that  8
on that day, there were 65 persons in the Centre. The 
Centre is registered with 20 number of beds.
20. The laudable object for enacting the Act need 
no reiteration. Mental illness is not something strange, it 
is like any other illness. The Act has intended to give 
dignity to the persons suffering from mental illness; the 
Act has further respected the dignity and privacy of a 
person suffering from mental illness; the Act has further 
regulated the admission of the persons in Mental 
Healthcare Establishment. There are specific provisions 
which deals with it. It may be a hazardous situation, if a 
person sound in mind without any mental illness, is 
confined in any institution or home or where persons with 
mental illness are confined. 
21. This Court in the case of Dr. Vijay Verma vs. 
Union of India and others, (2018) SCC Online 
Uttarakhand 519, has considered the implementation 
aspect of the Act in the State of Uttarakhand and in para 
52 of its judgment, number of directions have been given. 
What happened to those directions? 
22. Though the issue, at present, does not belong 
to the State of Uttarakhand, but reference has been made  9
to the incidents in District Dehradun and it is submitted 
on behalf of the learned counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand itself that this Court should examine the 
implementation aspect of the Act in the State of 
Uttarakhand. This Court considers to examine that 
aspect, as well.
23. The corpus Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav was 
detained by the Centre in contravention of the provisions 
of the Act. He had to remain for almost three months in 
the Centre. This act of the respondent no.6 may not be 
termed as a mistake. It is a question of liberty of a person 
snatched without in accordance with law. Mr. Vikas 
Singh Yadav has narrated the story of inhuman treatment 
and living conditions in the Centre. This Court does not 
know how far is that true. It may definitely be a matter of 
inquiry.
24. In view of the above, the Court issues the 
following directions:-
(i) The respondent no.3, SSP Moradabad, 
Uttar Pradesh shall conduct a detailed 
inquiry with regard to the working of the 
Centre. Let he be provided a copy of the 
paper-book and copies of all the 
documents, which have been given by  10
Mohd. Parvez on 30.11.2021 and the 
documents, which have been taken today 
in custody by this Court from Mohd. 
Parvez. After inquiry, respondent no.3, 
SSP Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh shall 
recommend action as permissible under 
law, including taking legal action against 
the persons, who are found to have
violated the provisions of the Act. 
(ii) The respondent no.6, Centre shall show 
cause, as to why the Centre should not be 
asked to award compensation to Mr. 
Vikas Singh Yadav for confining him for 
about three months in contravention of 
the provisions of law. 
(iii) Principal Secretary, Health, State of 
Uttarakhand, shall submit the followings;
(a) What action was taken by the State 
of Uttarakhand, pursuant to the 
directions issued by this Court in 
the case of Dr. Vijay Verma (supra).
(b) A list of such Mental Health 
Establishment, registered under 
the Act including any Centre in the 
name of Nasha Mukti Kendra, 
Rehabilitation Centre, etc. The list 
shall also contain the last three 
dates, when under Section 55 of  11
the Act, the State Authority 
supervised such establishments.
(c) When, in the last one year the 
meetings, of the State Authority,
constituted under the Act, took 
place. A copy of the resolutions of 
the State Authority shall also be 
enclosed. 
(iv) The Court also requests the respondent 
no.3 SSP Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh to 
submit a report of the action taken by him 
pursuant to this order. 
25. Let a copy of this order be sent to the Principal 
Secretary, Home, the State of Uttarakhand and Principal 
Secretary, Home, the State of Uttar Pradesh for ensuring 
that the provisions of the Act are implemented in the 
letter and spirt. 
26. The Court requests Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate,
who has represented the petitioner in the case, to assist

Habeas Corpus Petition No.22 of 2021
Bridjet Spencer ...Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ….Respondent
Present:-
Mr. D.S. Mehta, Amicus Curiae.

Mr. Pankaj Singh, Advocate for the respondent no.6.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
There are much larger issues involved in this 
petition now. It relates to the implementation of the Mental 
Health Care Act, 2017 (“the Act”). The Court has been seeking 
information from the Government of Uttarakhand on certain 
facts, particularly with regard to the directions issued by this 
Court in the case of Dr. Vijay Verma Vs. Union of India and 
others (2018) SCC Online Utt 519. By a communication dated 
11.02.2022, Secretary Health, Government of Uttarakhand has 
given a report. This report does not reveal much. It does not 
help the Court to understand as to what Health Department in 
the State is doing with regard to the implementation of the Act. 2
2. In Para 52 of the judgment, in the case of Dr. Vijay 
Verma (supra), the Court has issued various directions. The 
Court, today, perused the response of the Secretary Health. A 
direction in Para No. E is with regard to framing of a
comprehensive policy for rehabilitation of mentally disturbed 
children and patients. The Secretary Health replies that it does 
not belong to his department. The Court fails to understand as 
to what prevented the officer to collect the information, if he 
belongs to some other department and assist this Court in 
adjudicating this matter.
3. In Para 52 G, the Court had directed the State 
Government to conduct Epidemiological Survey data to 
determine the mentally retarded disturbed children. The report 
of Health Department, Government of Uttarakhand, reveals that 
a communication was sent to the concerned institute, which is 
dated 05.02.2022. The judgment, in the case of Dr. Vijay Verma, 
was delivered on 01.06.2018. The State Department slept over 
the directions for almost long four years. 
4. In Para 52 H of the judgment, in case of Dr. Vijay 
Verma (supra), the Court had required for establishment of 
Human Rights, Ethics, Law and Mental Health with certain 
objectives, as given in Para 40 of the judgment. For this purpose 
also, the Department of Health has made a communication on  3
05.02.2022. Government, on its own, has done nothing. They 
have not worked on it. They tried to outsource it. It is told that it 
has not yet been established. 
5. In Para 52 I of the judgment, in the case of Dr. 
Vijay Verma (supra), the Court had directed the State 
Government to constitute Mental Health Review Boards (“the 
Boards”). In fact, its composition is given in Section 73 of the 
Act. It includes an officer of the District Judiciary. Such Boards 
have not yet been constituted. The report of Health Department 
reveals that some directions for constitution of the Boards were 
issued in the year 2019 and in the year 2021. State Government 
is quite non-serious to the issue, which is in fact much 
important in the sphere of public health. The roles and duties of 
Boards are quite wide. Section 77 of the Act speaks of it. 
Proceedings of the Boards shall be judicial proceedings, as per 
Section 78 of the Act. There should be meetings of the Boards, 
as per Section 79 of the Act. Section 80 of the Act provides that 
the application, filed before the Boards, shall be decided within a 
period of 90 days. Section 82 of the Act gives wide powers to the 
Boards in the implementation of the provisions of the Act. The 
orders passed by the Boards are appealable to the High Court. It 
is most unfortunate that the Government of Uttarakhand has 
not constituted such Boards. Who is to be held responsible for 
it? Why should accountability be not fixed for it? Why the  4
Government be not asked to take actions against such officer, 
who were required to implement the provisions of the Act? This 
Court will consider this aspect at a later stage, if required.
6. During the course of argument, learned Amicus 
Curiae would suggest that the State Government should have 
data of persons suffering with mental illness. Only then, they 
could provide effective, adequate mental health care. He 
suggests that such data may be collected through Social 
Welfare Department, which provides for pensions to mentally 
challenged persons. It is submitted that based on such pension 
details, the persons could be examined, and thereafter, if 
required, adequate mental health care may be provided to such 
persons at an affordable cost.
7. Learned C.S.C. would submit that this data may be 
collected not only through Social Welfare Department, but 
through other health workers like Asha workers or ANMs, who 
are working in rural as well as city areas. He also suggests that 
the Chief Medical Officer/CMS Office may also provide the data 
on the subject. 
8. One more aspect needs little reference before the 
Court proceeds further. In Para 52 K of the judgment, in the 
case of Dr. Vijay Verma (supra), the Court had required State 
Government to provide Mental Health Care and Treatment at an  5
affordable cost of good quality, available in sufficient quantity, 
accessible geographically and without any discrimination. The 
reply says that somewhere near Dehradun, there is a centre in a 
hilly State of Uttarakhand with different geographical terrains. 
Can we say that one centre, near Dehradun, is geographically 
accessible to the persons suffering with mental illness? 
9. Learned C.S.C. would also submit that a 
communication has already been made to this Court through 
Secretary Law, Government of Uttarakhand for nominating an 
officer for constitution of the Boards. This Court has no doubt 
that this Court would promptly act to nominate the officers, in 
view of the provisions of the Act.
10. The Court expects that the data with regard to 
persons suffering from mental illness may be collected in a 
manner it is suggested today and it should be tabulated and it 
should also be indicated as to how such persons are getting 
mental health care at affordable cost.
11. Learned C.S.C. would submit that he has received 
some further instructions with regard to the implementation of 
the Act. He seeks for the time to compile all the information, 
with regard to implementation of the directions, as given in the 
case of Dr. Vijay Verma (supra) as also on the directions as 
issued by this Court in the instant petition. 6
12. Learned C.S.C. may file the report on or before 
15.07.2022. He will also share a copy of it with the learned 
Amicus Curiae.
13. Learned Amicus Curiae may thereafter submit his 
report on those points, if any, on or before 22.07.2022.
14. List this matter for hearing on 22.07.2022 as the first 
case.

5. Section 65(1) of the Mental 
Healthcare Act, 2017 ordains that no 
person or organisation shall establish or 
run a mental health establishment 
unless it has been registered with the 
Authority under the provisions of this 
Act. ‘Authority’, contemplated in Section 
65(1) of the Act, is to regulate the 
functioning of mental health 
establishments and various other 
matters. Section 65(6) of the said Act 
provides that the Authority shall, within 
a period of eighteen months from the 
commencement of the Act, by 
notification, specify the minimum 
standards for different categories of 
mental health establishments, and
period of eighteen months, mentioned in 
Section 65(6) of the Act, is to be 
reckoned from 08.01.2018, when the  Mental Healthcare Act was enforced. 
6. Section 121 of the Act confers Rule 
making power of Central and State 
Governments. Section 122 of the Act 
lays down the power of Central Authority 
to make Regulation; while, Section 123 
provides such powers upon the State 
Authority.
7. We are informed that the State of 
Uttarakhand is yet to notify the Rules in 
exercise of Rule-making power under 
Section 121 of the Act.
8. Learned counsel for petitioner 
submits that there is no regulatory 
framework in existence in Uttarakhand 
to regulate the standard and functioning 
of mental health establishments, due to 
which, persons with mental health are 
facing various problems and there are 
complaint of malpractices, which are 
surfacing every now and then.
9. Learned State Counsel, on 
instructions, submits that the Rules 
under Section 121 of the Act shall be 
notified, positively within ten days.
10. We, therefore, post this case on 
04.09.2023. 
11. In the meantime, if the Rules are 
not notified, the Secretary, Medical 
Health & Family Welfare, Uttarakhand 
shall appear in person before this Court, 
on the next date fixed. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
